analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction that the 0% promotional rate was withdrawn after a late payment and alleges financial loss of £212 interest, with a lack of explanation (CH-1).
analysis.summary: Mrs [PERSON_1] transferred a balance to her Harbourline credit card on an 18-month 0% deal. After one payment was two days late in July, the 0% rate was withdrawn and £212 interest charged. She says nobody explained one late payment would cancel the deal and that it is in the small print. She wants the 0% rate restored and the interest refunded. The handler notes T&Cs s.7.2 permit withdrawal and the key facts summary mentions it on p.3. Deadline 2026-11-24, At risk.

timeline.event: One card payment made two days late; 0% promotional rate withdrawn and £212 interest charged (as described by customer)
Handler reviewed T&Cs s.7.2 and key facts summary; noted contact preference letter and no vulnerability

analysis.severity_reason: Financial loss of £212 is between £100 and £1,000 under CH-6. No fraud, legal threat or vulnerability indicators identified.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None indicated. Note the handler recorded no vulnerability but does not say the customer was asked; offer support sensitively if contact is made.

analysis.routing_reason: No ESC-1 trigger: no fraud, lending decision or affordability issue, vulnerability referral, systemic issue, legal or media threat, or technical failure. The handler can resolve it; the decision on outcome rests with an authorised person.

policy_citations.how_it_applies: The £212 interest places the case in Medium severity.

policy_citations.quote: A late payment fee on a credit card is correctly charged if the minimum payment was not received by the due date.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Relevant to whether the late payment consequences were correctly applied; the complaint concerns withdrawal of the promo rate and interest, and checking for a bank-error Direct Debit failure is needed.

policy_citations.quote: Decisions on whether a complaint is upheld, and on any redress, must be made by an authorised complaints handler or specialist.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: No outcome is suggested here; a person must decide.

evidence.quote: Nobody explained that one late payment would cancel the whole deal
I want the 0% rate restored and the interest refunded.

handover.complaint_summary: Customer says her 0% balance transfer rate was ended and £212 interest charged after one payment was two days late in July, and that the consequence was not explained.
handover.desired_outcome: 0% rate restored and the interest refunded.
actions_taken: Handler reviewed T&Cs s.7.2 and key facts summary p.3
evidence_held: Credit card agreement and key facts
handover.vulnerability_assessment: No indicators found per handler note; MISSING whether the customer was asked about support needs.
open_questions: Why was the July payment late, and was a Direct Debit set up that failed (FEE-5)?
Was the payment received two days after the due date, and was the minimum amount paid?
Was the withdrawal of the promo rate applied correctly under the agreement?
Was the key facts summary provided to the customer at the outset?

other_gaps: Exact date and amount of the late payment not stated
Date the interest was charged not stated
analysis.suggested_next_step: Check the statements and Direct Debit history for the cause of the late payment, confirm the terms and how they were disclosed, send written acknowledgement if not yet sent, and have an authorised handler decide the outcome before 2026-11-24.
